column10: Q:SC3A. Social care in England is not free at the point of use. To get care funded by their council, someone must pass a needs assessment (how much care they need) and a means test (what they can afford).Anyone with savings and assets over £23,250 must pay for all their own care. Below this, costs are shared between the individual and their council on a sliding scale. The NHS may also contribute if someone has complex health needs.Overall, do you think this is a fair or unfair way to fund social care?
column13: Very fair
column14: Somewhat fair
